submissions.findingTextShort: An eight-week randomized trial of 400 mg/day L-ornithine reported selected stress, mood, and sleep-quality signals in mildly stressed healthy adults.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 52 mildly stressed or fatigued healthy Japanese adults tested 400 mg/day L-ornithine for eight weeks and reported changes in cortisol-related measures plus selected mood and sleep-quality outcomes. The findings belong to this healthy-worker/stress context and do not establish treatment efficacy for clinical anxiety or insomnia.
submissions.populationContext: 52 mildly stressed or fatigued healthy Japanese adults.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small population-specific study; substantial Kirin industry affiliation/provenance should remain visible during governed review.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2024 randomized stress-challenge trial found no salivary-cortisol improvement with L-ornithine despite selected next-morning mood/fatigue signals.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel trial in 65 healthy participants used 1600 mg/day L-ornithine for seven days with additional acute pre-TSST dosing. Salivary cortisol was not significantly improved, while selected next-morning fatigue-inertia and anger-hostility scores were more favorable. The null cortisol result must remain first-class and the acute laboratory-stress context must not be converted into clinical anxiety or sleep-treatment efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: 65 healthy participants exposed to a laboratory social-stress paradigm.
submissions.usageContext: L-ornithine 1600 mg/day for seven days plus acute pre-stress dosing.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Outcome disagreement and Kirin-affiliated provenance should remain explicit; subjective next-morning changes do not erase the primary physiologic null.
